channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh IT Company's AI Projects Highly Valued at UAE Energy Exhibition
item.description: Kazakhstan's TrustExam.ai presented its artificial intelligence platform for remote testing of oil and gas company employees at the ADIPEC 2026 exhibition in Abu Dhabi. The solution helps enterprises systematically verify knowledge in health, safety, and environmental protection (HSE), adapting to various production facilities and shift teams.

item.title: Group of Serial Cattle Rustlers Detained in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar Region
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Pavlodar region have detained a group of individuals suspected of serial cattle rustling. Over several months, the suspects allegedly committed more than five episodes of theft, stealing horses and cattle. During searches, stolen livestock and vehicles were recovered.

item.title: Uzbekistan Emergency Academy Hosts 'Meeting of Three Generations' for Cadets
item.description: The Academy of the Ministry of Emergency Situations in Uzbekistan organized a 'Meeting of Three Generations' to pass on experience from veterans to young servicemen. The academy chief emphasized the importance of generational continuity and fostering loyalty to the homeland. Recommendations were given on decisive action in complex situations.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Coxsackie Virus Not Registered as Separate Disease, Health Committee States
item.description: Uzbekistan's Sanitary-Epidemiological Committee, through representative Nurmat Otabekov, announced that the Coxsackie virus is not officially registered as a distinct illness. While often mild, the virus can cause complications like pneumonia and meningitis in some patients, according to the committee.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Belarus Agree to Strengthen Strategic Partnership and Discuss Eurasian Security
item.description: Kazakhstan and Belarus reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing political dialogue and bilateral cooperation. The countries signed a cooperation plan between their foreign ministries for 2027-2028. Discussions also covered Eurasian security, with Kazakhstan emphasizing mutual trust and international law.

item.title: US Midterm Elections Shape Central Asia's Economic and Diplomatic Agenda
item.description: Democrats' control of Congress following the US midterms inherits a Central Asia agenda focused on economic ties. Substantial orders for American manufacturers from Uzbekistan Airways and Kazakhstan's Wabtec agreement highlight the region's importance for US exports and jobs, influencing diplomatic engagement.

item.title: Shymkent Discusses Tasks Outlined in President's Address to the Nation
item.description: An active meeting in Shymkent, chaired by Mayor Gabit Syzdykbekov, discussed President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era." Participants, including officials and public figures, focused on strengthening the economy, modernizing infrastructure, and improving living standards.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Georgia Enhance Trade and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Tashkent's Deputy Khokim met with the Georgian Ambassador to discuss boosting trade, investment, and industrial cooperation. Emphasis was placed on increasing mutual trade volumes, launching new investment projects, and fostering direct contacts between entrepreneurs. Opportunities for Georgian companies in Tashkent's industrial zones and urban development were also explored.

item.title: Uzbek Students Participate in Space Experiments in Moscow
item.description: A team from Uzbekistan's Tashkent Institute of Irrigation and Agricultural Mechanization Engineers successfully presented a scientific-engineering project at the "ORBITA-2026" international space games in Moscow. The project involved studying the adaptation of living organisms to extreme conditions and performing tasks related to autonomous life support and engineering in simulated Martian missions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Agriculture Ministry Seeks Resumption of Enterprise Certification by Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Agriculture is seeking the resumption of certification for its enterprises by Russia's Rosselkhoznadzor. A meeting between veterinary service officials discussed further steps to ensure Kyrgyz products access to the Russian market, veterinary control, and the supply of veterinary medicines and biological preparations.

item.title: Trump Links Republican Election Losses to Iran War
item.description: US President Trump has acknowledged that the war with Iran partially influenced election results, contributing to Republican losses. However, he does not consider these defeats a personal political failure. The statement suggests a connection between foreign policy actions and domestic electoral outcomes.

item.title: Uzbek President to Visit Astana for Aqaba Process Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Astana on November 5-6 for an working visit at the invitation of Kazakhstan and Jordan leaders. He will participate in a meeting of Central Asian leaders within the Aqaba Process framework, discussing AI security and combating its misuse.

item.title: Iran's Supreme Leader Warns of Extensive Response to Further US Attacks
item.description: Iran's Supreme Leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, stated that Tehran's response to any future US attack would be more extensive. He reiterated that US hostility towards Iran would not change regardless of election results or concessions. Khamenei described actions against US bases and the Strait of Hormuz as part of Iran's campaign.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan Sign Treaty Elevating Relations to Allied Status
item.description: Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan have signed a Treaty on Allied Relations, establishing a legal framework for strategic partnership. This agreement deepens cooperation beyond traditional friendship, reflecting the leaders' vision. The treaty was signed in Tashkent on August 23, 2024, marking a new phase in bilateral ties.

item.title: Second Amur Tiger Released into the Wild in Kazakhstan's Ile-Balkhash Reserve
item.description: A second Amur tiger, a four-year-old male named Amur, has been released into the wild at the Ile-Balkhash reserve in the Almaty region. This initiative is part of a program to reintroduce tigers to Kazakhstan after a 70-year absence. The first tiger, Ümit, released in July, is adapting well.

item.title: Russia Attacks Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure; UN Condemns Actions
item.description: Russian forces conducted aerial attacks on Ukraine's energy facilities. The United Nations condemned these strikes as violations of international humanitarian law, urging an immediate ceasefire. Following a Ukrainian drone strike, a warehouse at the Ozon marketplace in Adygeysk, Russia, caught fire.

item.title: Uzbek President to Visit Astana for Central Asian Leaders' Meeting
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay a working visit to Astana on November 5-6. He will participate in a meeting of Central Asian state leaders within the framework of the Aqaba process. The visit aims to foster regional cooperation and dialogue.

item.title: Experts Discuss Kazakhstan President's Address on Development Priorities
item.description: Experts in Almaty convened to discuss the key points of the President's address on state and public development. They analyzed the potential impact of proposed initiatives on the economy and social sphere, with a focus on infrastructure modernization and increasing public income.

item.title: Bishkek Electricity Network Undergoing Civil Defense Readiness Assessment
item.description: From November 4-6, the Bishkek Electricity Network is undergoing an assessment of its civil defense readiness. Specialists are evaluating the enterprise's preparedness for emergencies, communication systems, resource availability, and staff training levels. Attention is focused on rapid response capabilities.

item.title: UN Warns of Widening Gap in Afghanistan's Education System by 2026
item.description: The UN projects a significant gap between rising demand and limited capacity in Afghanistan's education system by 2026. Population growth, crises, underinvestment, and migrant returns are increasing pressure. Over a million people, including 245,000 children, returned in 2026, exacerbating the strain on schools and services. Millions of girls remain denied education beyond sixth grade.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Experts Discuss Labor Rights and Legal Literacy
item.description: A new episode of the "AdvoKast" project in Uzbekistan focuses on labor relations, emphasizing the importance of understanding labor laws. Experts discussed what to consider when starting a job, the procedure for formalizing employment contracts, and the rights and obligations of employers and employees. Ignorance of labor legislation can lead to serious consequences.

item.title: Head of 'SQ-Pharma' Nurlybek Asylbekov Becomes Vice Minister of Healthcare
item.description: Nurlybek Asylbekov, who led 'SQ-Pharma' since 2025, has been appointed Vice Minister of Healthcare of Kazakhstan. The government's press service announced the appointment. Asylbekov has held various leadership and expert positions in the pharmaceutical industry, regional administration, and the Ministry of Health.

item.title: Uzpromstroybank Enters New Development Phase, Targeting International Capital Markets
item.description: Uzpromstroybank (SQB) is entering a new phase of development focused on sustainable and secure growth, moving beyond a model solely focused on current income. The bank's assets have reached 104 trillion soums, and its deposit base has grown 2.7 times. While profits show fluctuations, the bank emphasizes institutional transformations and expansion into international capital markets.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Urges Head of "SK-Farmatsiya" to Work Honestly
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has again called on the head of "SK-Farmatsiya" to work honestly, emphasizing that corruption must not be tolerated in the spending of any funds. He stated that honest work would lead to positive results. The call highlights ongoing concerns about integrity within the pharmaceutical procurement system.

item.title: Kazakhstan Farmers Discuss Business Profitability at IX Agroforum
item.description: The IX Agroforum, organized by KMF Bank and the KMF-Demey Corporate Fund in Turkestan, brought together 800 participants to discuss enhancing agricultural business profitability. Topics included yield increase, cost optimization, and access to financing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Releases National Media Consumption Research Findings
item.description: Uzbekistan has published the results of its first national media consumption study in many years, conducted by the National Mass Media Support and Development Public Fund, the EU Delegation, and the 'Ijtimoiy fikr' Center. The research surveyed residents across all 14 regions, including rural areas.

item.title: Astana Businessman Sentenced to Over Six Years for Parachute Supply Fraud
item.description: A businessman in Astana has been sentenced to six years and eight months in prison for embezzling 646 million tenge allocated for parachute supplies to the military. The company head signed a contract with the state enterprise "Kazspetsexport" but failed to deliver the goods after receiving an advance payment. The court found the entrepreneur guilty of large-scale fraud.

item.title: Bishkek Hands Over Keys to 530 Apartments in Karakol Housing Complex
item.description: Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliyev presented keys to 530 apartments in the "Khan-Teniri" housing complex in Karakol. These units were built by the State Mortgage Company as part of the second phase of development. The overall complex aims to include 3,430 apartments across 69 blocks, along with social infrastructure like a kindergarten and school.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches Wastewater Treatment and Water Supply Systems in 70 Villages
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has launched modern wastewater treatment and drinking water supply systems in 70 villages across seven regions. This initiative, supported by $567.5 million in investments since 2021, has provided over 663,000 citizens with access to quality drinking water. The project emphasizes ecological safety, particularly for Lake Issyk-Kul, and supports regional tourism development.

item.title: 16 Kyrgyz Pasture Communities Receive Grants for Infrastructure Improvement
item.description: Sixteen pasture communities in Kyrgyzstan will receive over 43.4 million soms in grants to improve pasture infrastructure, restore watering points, repair bridges and roads, and fence pastures. These projects, part of the 'Resilience of Regional Pasture Communities - ADAPT' project funded by IFAD, aim to enhance climate resilience and sustainable land management.

item.title: Minor Detained with Brass Knuckles in Almaty Metro
item.description: A 17-year-old minor was apprehended in the Almaty metro carrying an item resembling brass knuckles. Police are investigating the origin, ownership, and purpose of the confiscated item. The teenager was handed over to the district police for further proceedings.

item.title: Uzbekistan Deepens Cooperation with UN on Anti-Corruption Efforts
item.description: Uzbekistan's delegation is participating in the 15th meeting of the Open-ended Intergovernmental Working Group on Asset Recovery in Vienna. The discussions focus on applying the UN Convention against Corruption and strengthening cooperation, including legal assistance and asset recovery. Bilateral meetings with European countries are also planned.

item.title: Central Asian Republics to Coordinate Climate Agenda at COP31 in Türkiye
item.description: Central Asian nations will participate in COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, from November 9-20. Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan will lead efforts to coordinate regional messaging and environmental priorities. Key discussions will focus on cooperation, joint climate initiatives, glacier retreat, water security, and climate finance mobilization.

item.title: Kazakhstan's TrustExam.ai Technology Project Showcased at UAE Energy Conference
item.description: Kazakhstan's TrustExam.ai technology project presented its remote examination platform for oil and gas company employees and contractors at the ADIPEC 2026 international energy exhibition in Abu Dhabi. The platform aims to systematically verify knowledge in health, safety, and environmental protection, integrating testing, biometrics, and AI-based proctoring.

item.title: Former Head of "SK-Pharmacy" Appointed Vice Minister of Healthcare in Kazakhstan
item.description: Nurlybek Assylbekov, former chairman of "SK-Pharmacy", has been appointed Vice Minister of Healthcare of Kazakhstan. Additionally, Ainur Abdyrakhmanova became Vice Minister of Labor and Social Protection, and Yulia Ovechkina was appointed head of the Committee for the Protection of Children's Rights.

item.title: Aqaba Process summit to be held in Astana on November 6
item.description: The Aqaba Process summit is scheduled to take place in Astana on November 6. This international meeting will bring together leaders and representatives to discuss regional security and cooperation.

item.title: Fraudsters opened bank card in Kazakh woman's name, leading to criminal case
item.description: Fraudsters allegedly used a Kazakh woman's personal identification number to open a bank card in her name and conduct illegal transactions. The woman now faces a criminal investigation for actions she did not commit, with her accounts frozen.

item.title: US judge temporarily blocks deportation of Afghan nationals to Afghanistan or Pakistan
item.description: A federal judge in New York has temporarily blocked the U.S. government from deporting Afghan nationals to Afghanistan or Pakistan. The order, effective until November 7, was issued due to concerns that detainees could face persecution under Taliban rule.

item.title: Uzbekistan Ministry and Prosecutor's Office Deny Mandatory Student App Installation
item.description: Reports emerged of students in Tashkent being forced to install the 'Xavfsiz Talaba' app. The university rector stated a directive was received from the prosecutor's office. However, the Ministry of Higher Education and the Prosecutor's Office later clarified that installing the app is not mandatory.

item.title: Uzbekistan Interior Minister Addresses Citizen Complaints in Extended Reception
item.description: Uzbekistan's Interior Minister, Aziz Toshpo'latov, held a personal reception for citizens on October 31, which lasted until 11 PM. Of the 481 complaints registered, 236 were resolved on the spot, while the remaining 245 require further investigation.
